Vendor statement reconciliation

Ties a supplier's own statement to your accounts payable, item by item, to find invoices your books never saw and credit notes nobody claimed.

Watch someone use it

Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading and Harbor Office Supply, account NB-2210, statement dated 25 September. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

Claudewith the MosoFin vendor statement reconciliation skill

Harbor Office Supply sent us a statement. Can you check it against our books?

Claude

Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.

  1. Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload files?
  2. Please attach Harbor's statement, as a PDF or CSV. I always need it, because MosoFin cannot read it.
  3. Which company is the statement addressed to, and what account reference does it show?
  4. What is your cutoff date? What date is on the statement?
  5. Does the statement list every open item, only overdue items, or a balance brought forward?
  6. Do you keep a dispute log? Are you holding back any invoices on purpose?
  7. Which suppliers do you reconcile, how often, and who owns the exceptions?

Use MosoFin. Statement attached. It's addressed to Northbrook Trading, account NB-2210. Our books are at 30 September, the statement is dated 25 September. It lists every open item. No disputes. We do Harbor monthly, and AP owns the exceptions.

📄 harbor-statement-25-september.pdf

  1. list_workspacesNorthbrook Trading
  2. get_agent_datasourcesNorthbrook Trading, the statement's addressee
  3. get_datasource_toolsRead tools only

The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

Claude

Here is my plan. I reconcile Harbor Office Supply's open-item statement to Northbrook Trading's supplier ledger, account reference NB-2210. I read the ledger and payments through MosoFin.

Your cutoff is 30 September and the statement is dated 25 September. So I reconcile at 25 September, and I list each ledger item from 26 to 30 September on its own. Shall I start?

Yes, go ahead.

  2. Harbor's ledger, to today$21,115.00 at 30 Sep

7 reads in one batch, past your cutoff. Nothing in your books changed.

Claude

I matched Harbor's lines to your ledger, document number first. INV-0042 on the statement is document 42 in your books. Then I took your ledger back to the statement date:

Your ledger at the statement date
Your ledger at 30 Sep$21,115.00
− Invoice 0057, dated 27 Sep$3,100.00
+ Your payment of 29 Sep$625.00
= Your ledger at 25 Sep$18,640.00

Both items are timing. Harbor shows them on its next statement.

Claude

Harbor's statement says $20,710.00. Two of its lines are not in your books:

Your ledger to Harbor's statement, 25 Sep
Your ledger at 25 Sep$18,640.00
+ INV-0049, 18 Sep, not in your books$2,480.00
− Credit note CN-0011, 12 Sep, not in your books$410.00
= Expected statement balance$20,710.00
Harbor's statement at 25 Sep$20,710.00
Unexplained$0.00

INV-0049 matches nothing in your books at any tier. It is not under a second Harbor record or in a sibling company. So it is a possible bill you never recorded. Please ask Harbor for a copy.

Claude

Harbor also owes you money. CN-0011 is a credit for returned chairs. It relates to INV-0031, which you paid in full on 5 September.

Money owed to you
INV-0031$410.00
− Paid on 5 Sep$410.00
= Still owed on INV-0031$0.00
+ CN-0011, not taken$410.00
= Cash Harbor owes you$410.00

You have no open Harbor bill, so the credit has nothing to go against. Ask Harbor for a refund, or take it off the next bill. Did you receive the INV-0049 goods and return those chairs?

Yes. We got the goods, and we returned the chairs. Both are real.

Claude

Thank you. I propose one entry now:

Proposed entry, not posted
EntryAmountEvidence
Accrual at 30 Sep: debit expense or inventory, credit accrued liabilities$2,480.00INV-0049 on Harbor's statement, and your yes

The accrual reverses on 1 October. When the invoice copy arrives, the invoice takes its place. A statement line does not support a credit entry, so please ask Harbor for the CN-0011 document too. A person posts entries and contacts Harbor. I do neither.

Claude

Your workpaper has six sheets: the summary, the matched items with their tier, the exceptions, the proposed entry, the supplier ranking and the coverage. AP owns both exceptions. Please give each one a target date.

Do you want the workpaper as an Excel file?
